summary_paragraph: A woman with complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later open reversal and gastrostomy history), chronic abdominal pain, anxiety/depression, and recent second recurrence of C. difficile on an oral vancomycin taper was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting with poor oral intake, frequent diarrhea, and dehydration. Evaluation showed stable vital signs, no leukocytosis, normal lactate, and CT abdomen/pelvis without acute intra-abdominal process. Stool testing during this admission was negative for toxigenic C. difficile and negative for common bacterial pathogens and parasites. She improved with IV fluids, antiemetics, and pain control, with resolution of in-hospital vomiting and decreased diarrhea, and was able to tolerate oral intake by discharge. She was discharged home to continue the previously prescribed vancomycin taper with GI follow-up, and propranolol was held due to asymptomatic low blood pressure; pending cultures were to be followed as an outpatient.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
